history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed (Buddhist monastery). One of Sikkim's oldest monasteries, on a ridge above Pelling ~7 km from Pemayangtse; founding-date conflict — most travel sources give 1697 by Lama Lhatsun Chempo (Gyalwa Lhatsum Chempo), while Wikipedia lists 1701 by Lhatsün Namkha Jikmé (verify). The name means 'Island of the Guhyamantra (secret-mantra/Vajrayana) teachings'. The original structure was devastated by fire and later rebuilt. The monastery holds 17th-century clay statues among the oldest in the region plus wall paintings, scriptures and other artefacts, and is reached by a steep 4-km forest track.

name: Sangachoeling Monastery
town_description: Pelling is a hill town in West Sikkim at about 2,150 m, known for close views of Kanchenjunga and as the base for the Rabdentse ruins, Pemayangtse and Sanga Choeling monasteries, Khecheopalri Lake, and the Pelling Sky Walk.

travel.road: Hill-top ridge ~7 km from Pemayangtse, ~4 km steep trek from Pelling through forest; Pelling itself is ~140 km west of Gangtok
